# Mew Assistant – AI Coding Guide

- **Purpose & entrypoints:** FastAPI app boots in [app/main.py](app/main.py) with lifespan calling [app/database/connection.py](app/database/connection.py) `init_db()` (no Alembic). Routers live in [app/routers](app/routers) and are mounted with prefixes (`/auth`, `/calendar`, `/mew`, `/voice`, `/mobile`, `/approvals`).
- **Auth/JWT:** JWT/Argon2 helpers in [app/utils/auth.py](app/utils/auth.py); access tokens default to 30 days (`ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRE_MINUTES`) and refresh tokens carry `type=refresh`. Always depend on `get_current_user` instead of manual header parsing.
- **OAuth flows:** Two deliberately separate, unrelated flows. (1) Sign-in is entirely [app/routers/oauth_workos.py](app/routers/oauth_workos.py) (`/auth/workos/*`), a thin wrapper around [WorkOS AuthKit](https://workos.com/docs/authkit) via [app/services/workos_client.py](app/services/workos_client.py) — hosted UI, no per-provider code in this app, sets an HttpOnly session cookie. (2) [app/routers/calendar_oauth.py](app/routers/calendar_oauth.py) (`/calendar-sync/google/*`) is a completely separate Google Cloud OAuth client used only for a parent granting Mew read access to a provider's Google Calendar once already signed in — not a sign-in path. Don't conflate the two, and don't look for `oauth.py`/`oauth_simple.py`; neither exists in this tree.
- **Three-persona scheduling (core surface):** one schedule shared by a parent (or guardian — the same handlers answer on both `/parent` and `/guardian` prefixes), a kid, and a service provider. `POST /requests` ([app/routers/requests.py](app/routers/requests.py)) is the *only* write path for a kid or provider's proposed change; a client never decides what's allowed. Every request is evaluated by the deterministic `RuleEngine` ([app/services/rule_engine.py](app/services/rule_engine.py)) — pure, no DB, no AI. A request that satisfies every active rule is applied immediately and logged quietly; one that doesn't reaches the parent as a pending `ApprovalRequest` with reason codes and three compliant alternatives, resolved via `POST /parent/approvals/{id}/choose`. Providers get their own scoped view via `GET /provider/sessions`. See [docs/THREE_PERSONA_SCHEDULING.md](docs/THREE_PERSONA_SCHEDULING.md) for the full loop and code map.
- **Calendar web/demo:** Lightweight calendar page at [app/routers/calendar_web.py](app/routers/calendar_web.py) and API proxy in [app/routers/simple_calendar.py](app/routers/simple_calendar.py); tokens are read from query/localStorage and sent as Bearer. Avoid breaking these demo pages when touching auth headers or paths.
- **Data model highlights:** See [app/database/models.py](app/database/models.py) for enums and tables. Important: `ApprovalRequest` enforces parent review before kid actions (`applied_to_calendar` guarded, indices by kid/parent/status); `APIKey` stores hashed keys + prefixes; `ScheduleEntry` tracks recurrence, external calendar IDs, and priority/status enums; voice tracking via `VoiceCommand`/`VoiceSession`; caregiver summaries in `CaregiverSummary`. Keep cascade relationships (`User.sessions/messages/api_keys/federated_identities`) intact.
- **Service layer:** Keep routers thin—business logic in [app/services](app/services) (auth, calendar, approval, kid, voice, AI scheduler). Reuse services instead of duplicate queries; many services are stubs, so add TODOs when only partially implementing.
- **Schemas:** Pydantic models in [app/schemas](app/schemas) must stay aligned with router signatures to keep `/docs` accurate. Update schemas when changing payloads instead of patching OpenAPI by hand.
- **Middleware & errors:** Shared middleware in [app/middleware.py](app/middleware.py); only CORS is mounted by default. Use `MewException` from [app/utils/exceptions.py](app/utils/exceptions.py) for consistent JSON errors. Logger helper is in [app/utils/logger.py](app/utils/logger.py).
- **Environment:** Copy [.env.example](.env.example) -> `.env`. Set `DATABASE_URL` (Postgres default, SQLite works for dev), `JWT_SECRET_KEY`, and OAuth client IDs/secrets (`GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID/SECRET`, `MICROSOFT_CLIENT_ID/SECRET`, `BASE_URL`). Long-lived tokens are intentional for federated logins—don’t shorten without product sign-off.
- **Run/build:** `make install` then `make dev` (uvicorn 0.0.0.0:8000). Alt: `uvicorn app.main:app --reload --port 8888`. DB for dev via `make db-up` (Podman) or switch to SQLite URL. Containers: `docker build -t mew-assistant .` then `docker run -p 8888:8000 --env-file .env mew-assistant`.
- **Testing & lint:** `make test` or `pytest -v tests/`; coverage via `make test-cov`. Linters/formatters: `make lint` (flake8, mypy) and `make format` (black, isort). Several bash harnesses (`test_api.sh`, `test_auth.sh`, `test_ai_endpoints.sh`) expect a running server.
- **API docs:** Live `/docs` when server is up; static spec in [openapi.json](openapi.json). Keep routers/schemas in sync rather than editing the spec directly.
- **Deployment:** [Fly.io](https://fly.io) via [fly.toml](fly.toml) (app `mew-assistant`, region `iad`) — the CI/CD pipeline's `deploy_fly` job (`.github/workflows/ci-cd.yml`) runs `flyctl deploy --remote-only` on push to `master` once tests/lint/security/secret-scan all pass, then polls `/health`. The repo also still has dormant, no-longer-wired-in Azure IaC (`infrastructure/azure/`, root `*.bicep` files) kept for reference/teardown only — don't resurrect it without checking with the repo owner first.
- **Data flow pattern:** request -> router -> service -> models -> response schema. Calendar/voice/mobile features often need federated tokens from `FederatedIdentity`/`OAuthProvider` rows—avoid returning raw tokens to clients.
- **Gotchas:** Demo/simple routers are customer-facing; keep paths and query param names stable. Token TTLs are long by design. No migrations tool; schema changes must update models and rely on startup `create_all()` or add SQL scripts in repo.

If any section needs more depth (e.g., full OAuth redirect URI rules, DB table semantics, or deployment steps), say so and I’ll tighten it further.
